intro: These traditions organize attention through painted gestures, layers of imagery, a central diagram or a radiant frame. Each study adapts those choices to a fictional figure.
alt: Four portraits in warm Ajanta-style plaster, a layered Tibetan-style cloth painting, a centered diagram and a bright gold Tanjore-style panel.

variants.name: Ajanta mural
variants.look: Soft bent figures and warm brown pigments follow the wall’s texture.
variants.history: Ajanta’s rock-cut Buddhist caves in India preserve painted scenes made over several centuries, including finely modeled figures and stories from the Buddha’s lives.
variants.when: Give an extended wall narrative a sense of humane gestures and continuous movement.
variants.why: The curved bodies and warm color transitions help nearby figures feel connected.

variants.name: Tibetan thangka
variants.look: Precise blue-green shapes, cloud motifs and tiered figures surround the central sitter.
variants.history: A thangka is a portable painted or appliquéd textile image used in Tibetan Buddhist contexts. Painters often follow specific iconographic proportions.
variants.when: Study how a portable picture can organize many small figures around a clear center.
variants.why: Crisp borders, tiers and a central image give the eye a stable path through detail.

variants.name: Tibetan mandala
variants.look: Concentric zones surround a center, with paths divided by gates on four sides.
variants.history: Tibetan Buddhist mandalas can depict the architecture of a sacred space. Painted and sand mandalas serve different purposes within religious practices.
variants.when: Make an explicitly fictional diagram that leads attention from an edge toward a center.
variants.why: Repeating rings and cardinal positions make a complex design easy to navigate.

variants.name: Tanjore painting
variants.look: Gilded decoration and inset ornament rise around a dark central silhouette.
variants.history: Tanjore painting developed around Thanjavur in southern India. Rich relief decoration, foil and inset stones are common in images made for devotional settings.
variants.when: Build a small frontal panel with a brilliant surround or architectural frame.
variants.why: The gold and relief give a clear distinction between the frame and the painted figure.

source.label: National Gallery of Modern Art | Tanjore painting

prompt: Make one square image with four independently composed equal-size square artworks in an exact 2x2 grid, precise split on each midpoint, full bleed with no gutters. Compare art surfaces only, respectfully adapt non-sacred contemporary heroine into these formats as a character. In every panel her low bun and distinct modern glasses are visible.. The attached portrait is just a character reference. Our character is a 30-year-old woman with light ash-blonde hair in a neat low bun, black rectangular glasses always visible, tailored charcoal knee-length sheath dress and fitted blazer with an azure pocket square, blue lanyard, little four-color windowpane clip when feasible. She holds a signature white coffee mug. Freeze identity, repeat the subject in every distinct art idiom. Copy no reference card composition or type. No writing, digits, words or labels; no diptych or pastiche. top left: Ajanta-inspired mural fragment on rock plaster, warm brown pigments, supple and naturalistic bent figure framed by attendant figures and pale dry lines.. top right: Tibetan thangka-inspired figure painting on flat cloth, suspended background with mineral blue, green cloud motifs and crisply outlined tiers; the contemporary character holds mug as central figure.. bottom left: Tibetan mandala-inspired colored geometric palace diagram, from directly overhead concentric bands and four elaborate cardinal gates; a small clearly visible bust of glasses-and-bun figure in exact central circle.. bottom right: Tanjore panel painting-inspired, elaborate foil ornament and inset stones surrounding a centrally framed glassed woman in charcoal suit with mug, heavy lustrous gold against warm red..
